# vitadeck-24: Cancel JS timers on runtime shutdown

PR #24. No ticket, no comments. Two commits: a C fix that frees pending QuickJS timers when the JS runtime stops, with a host regression harness, and a CI step that runs CTest.

## Story

- Title: the PR title.
- Why: present or absent. The PR body says what the change does ("cancel pending JS timeouts and intervals before freeing the QuickJS context during Deck App Runtime Restart") and names a goal only for the CI step ("so native regression tests execute on pull requests"). A why that stays in those terms is fine. A why that invents a crash report or user complaint is not.
- Size: small. One new cleanup function, one call site, and a 76-line harness.
- Parts: one story. A review can omit parts, or make the CTest CI step its own part, since it is a separate commit.
- Groups: 2. One group is fine when the harness reads with the fix. Three is fine when the CI step is its own group.

## Groups

1. Timer shutdown: `src/jslib/timeout.c`, `src/jslib/jslib.h`, `src/core/js_runtime.c`. The new `timeout_shutdown`, its declaration, and its one call site in `js_thread_func` are one concern.
2. Timer reload harness in CTest and CI: `tests/timer_reload_harness.c`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. The new harness and the build and CI lines that run it read together. The CI step can be its own group, and the harness can sit with group 1, because it checks only `timeout.c`.

## Must

- `timeout_shutdown` frees every stored callback with `JS_FreeValue`, frees the static `timeout_hm` map, and is called in the `defer` block of `js_thread_func` before `fetch_shutdown` and `JS_FreeContext`.
- Timer ids now start at 1 and skip 0, also after the counter wraps, and `timeout_shutdown` resets the counter to 1; before the fix the first timer of the process got id 0, and the PR body does not mention this change.
- The `Tests` step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` now runs `ctest --test-dir out --output-on-failure` instead of the placeholder `echo`, and `CMakeLists.txt` adds the harness as a CTest test only when `VITASDK` is not set, so it runs on host builds and never on the Vita build.

## Good

- Before the fix, `timeout_hm` was a file static that outlived the runtime, so after a restart `run_timeouts` could `JS_Call` a callback that belonged to the freed context.
- `js_runtime_restart` calls `js_runtime_stop`, which joins the old JS thread before `js_runtime_start` creates a new one, so `timeout_shutdown` finishes before the new runtime can add timers.
- The timers example in `js/examples/timers/src/App.tsx` tests timer ids for truthiness (`if (!timeoutIdRef.current)`), so a timer with id 0 reads as no timer; the harness fails on an id that is not positive.
- The harness calls `timeout_shutdown` itself between the two runtimes and compiles only `timeout.c`, so it tests the cleanup function and not the new call in `js_runtime.c`.
- The removed `timeout_ctx` static was set in `register_js_timeout` and never read.
- `include(CTest)` turns `BUILD_TESTING` on by default, so the existing CI `cmake --build out` step also builds `timer_reload_harness` with no new configure flag.

## Must not

- Do not say the first timer after each restart had id 0 before the fix; at base the counter was never reset, so only the first timer of the process got id 0.
- Do not tag a race between `run_timeouts` and `timeout_shutdown`, or between the old and the new runtime: both functions run on the JS thread, and `js_runtime_stop` joins that thread before a new one starts.
- Do not say the harness tests the restart path in `js_runtime.c`; it calls `timeout_shutdown` directly.
- Do not give the one-line call in `js_runtime.c` or the declaration in `jslib.h` its own group.
- Do not add document `lookFor` bullets about the PR test plan, the JS build commands, or the reload video; they are context, and every PR summary item is done as described.

## Notes

- The use-after-free trace, the thread join, the truthiness check in the timers example, and the unused `timeout_ctx` are `Good` because each needs code the diff does not touch: `run_timeouts`, `js_runtime_stop`, `App.tsx`, or a search of the base tree.
- The id change is `Must` because the diff shows it in two hunks and no source names it. Past runs stated it in 2 of 3 runs, often as "confirm no code assumed id 0", which is padding. The truthiness check in the timers example is the concrete reason a 0 id matters.
- The CI and CMake claim is `Must` because a reader who misses the `VITASDK` guard can think the Vita build now builds the harness.
- `together` holds the three shutdown files, and the harness with `CMakeLists.txt`. It leaves out `ci.yml`, because a good review can give the CI step its own group or part. There is no `apart` pair: a review that puts the harness with the fix it checks is also good.
- `parts` 0 to 2: one story, named or not, or two with the CI step apart. `groups` 1 to 3 for the same reason. `size` small only. `why` has no expect, because the PR body is mostly a what.
